arms.note: VERDICT 2026-09-23 15:00: fix CONFIRMED as crash-cure — clean train descent to 2.875, no eval nulls, no plateau, guard fired properly. But capacity answer is NO: best 1.5890 @2100 (~69M tok), early-stop at 4700 (val 1.8546 > best+15% while TRAIN still falling = classic overfit-at-hot-LR mid-schedule, NOT a collapse). 160M still loses to 70M champion 1.4699@12000. Pattern across all three 50k long arms: val bottoms at 130-2400 steps then climbs while train descends; the 70M's improvement lived in its ANNEALING phase (lr decay after step ~7000) — neither 160M arm ever got there before the guard aborted it. Next hypothesis: schedule-length, not size. Collision note (attempt 1/1312) kept below.

arms.goal: Pythia-70M shape on the FULL 2.0B-token Pile diet, one epoch, to measure the open-weights gap vs EleutherAI/pythia-70m under the same corpus/encoder. Pythia saw 300B tokens; this sees 2.0B (0.67%) - the gap is the finding.
arms.note: ABORTED BY OPERATOR at step ~6200 (2026-09-29 21:57). NEGATIVE RESULT at lr 5e-4, not debris. Val climbed 4 consecutive evals: 1.9683 (3k) -> 1.9980 (4k) -> 2.0677 (5k) -> 2.1314 (6k) while train loss fell 4.58 -> 3.49: train/val gap widening from step 3000. Leading indicators confirm the hot-LR signature: gnorm 0.37->0.99, lmax 7.9->11.3, ent 7.3->3.9. Same failure shape as the 2026-09-27 OWT run at 1.5e-3 (floor reached ~step 2300, then eaten). The 1.30 degrade guard would not have tripped until ~step 11000, so the schedule would have burned ~3h before self-stopping. CONCLUSION: 5e-4 is still too hot for this corpus/ctx even with a cosine decay to 10% - the endgame it was designed to reach is unreachable if the floor is destroyed in the first 5k steps. Next arm halves to 2.5e-4.

arms.goal: Same full-diet Pile arm at lr 2.5e-4 (half of 5e-4). The 5e-4 arm reached best bpb 1.9683 @ step 3000 then regressed 4 consecutive evals to 2.1314 by step 6000 with the train/val gap widening +0.05 -> +2.33; gnorm up, ent down. Test whether halving the peak keeps the floor alive long enough for the cosine endgame.
arms.note: ABORTED BY OPERATOR at step ~8100 (2026-09-29 22:31). NEGATIVE RESULT, and the decisive one: val turns over at the SAME ~4k place as the 5e-4 control, only shallower. best bpb 2.0132 @ 4000, then 2.0194 (5k), 2.0550 (6k), 2.1154 (7k), 2.1917 (8k). TWO LRs A FACTOR OF 2 APART, BOTH TURN OVER AT 3-4k STEPS. CONCLUSION: the knee is LR-INDEPENDENT on this corpus. The lever is not LR - it is data volume (2.0B tokens) or model capacity (70M), and no third LR rung will move the knee. Do not spend 8h on one. NEXT: score EleutherAI/pythia-70m on the same held-out tail to get the open-weights gap, then attack with data or size, not LR.

arms.goal: Knee probe at eff batch 131,072 (micro 16 x accum 16), LR held at 5e-4. Single-lever vs pile-full-diet-70m: ONLY eff_batch changes 16,384 -> 131,072. Both killed LR arms showed `served` RISING after the knee (model stops fitting its own training batches = steps too large, not overfitting) and both gaps flat, so the lever is step noise, not LR and not data. 5,000 steps = 655M tokens = 9.26 tok/param = 13x the control's 0.69 tok/param knee point.
arms.note: COMPLETED 2026-09-30 11:43 PDT, all 5,000 steps, no early stop, no degrade-guard abort. BEST val bpb 1.53965 @ step 5000 (4.1732 nats) = 655,360,000 tokens = 9.26 tok/param. It never turned over: served loss kept RISING against val, so the batch lever held all the way to the ceiling of this probe. THE CONFIRMED WIN - eff batch 16,384 -> 131,072 moved the knee from 0.69 tok/param to past 9.26 (13x), and best bpb 1.9683 -> 1.5396 (-0.429). THE THIRD LEVER IS RETIRED: lr 5e-4 and 2.5e-4 turned over at the SAME ~3-4k steps on the eff-16k arm, so lr was never the variable. CONFIG CHOICE (measured, not guessed): micro 32 x accum 8 hit 16,001MB of 16,376MB = 98% of the card and thrashed the allocator down to 18,556 tok/s; micro 16 x accum 16 = 12,017MB at 77,464 tok/s - 8x the effective batch AND faster. Logits are batch x ctx x vocab, so MICRO-batch drives VRAM while accumulation is free. The full epoch that follows drops dropout 0.1 -> 0.0 (commit a966f1e, EleutherAI parity) and stretches the cosine 3x, so it is NOT a clean single-lever read against this probe.

arms.goal: FULL EPOCH over the Pile at Pythia-70M parity: one pass over the 2,003,992,003-token cache = 15,136 steps at eff batch 131,072 (micro 16 x accum 16), ctx 512, dropout 0.0, lr 5e-4 cosine. TARGET IS CHINCHILLA, not pythia-70m's 1.2727: 20 tok/param = step 10,794 predicts ~1.36 bpb; pass mark ~1.42 bpb at step 10,794. pythia-70m saw 4,258 tok/param (212x Chinchilla, 300B tokens), so its number is an ASYMPTOTE, not a reachable target.
arms.note: TWO LAUNCH ATTEMPTS ON ONE ARM. (1) 20260930_1143 ABORTED BY OPERATOR at step 856 (~19 min GPU) so Shane could use the card; curve kept at runs/20260930_1143_pythia_tokenizer_pile_train_full/loss.jsonl (val bpb 2.0138 @600, 1.9785 @800, still descending). Its numbers are NOT comparable to the 5k probe - the probe's cosine was fully cooled by step 5,000 while this attempt was still at ~5.0e-4, so the hotter LR is schedule position, not a regression. (2) 20260930_2055 RESTARTED FRESH at step 0 rather than resuming the aborted weights, because a mid-cosine resume would restart the LR schedule against a stale early-stop ledger. Do NOT compare this arm's step-5000 to the probe's 1.5396: same tokens seen, but the cosine here is stretched over 15,136 so LR is still ~3.9e-4 at step 5,000. Compare final-to-final. GRADED READING: a small constant offset (+0.16 to +0.22 nats vs the Chinchilla fit, shrinking) is expected from a population regression; a GROWING gap is the failure mode and is what killed the eff-16k arm. Disk: checkpoints already 163G, D: has 1.15TB free, this run adds ~21G. ||| VERDICT 2026-10-02 (Lisa, from runs/20260930_2055 + reports/matched_tokens_70m.json): PASS. Attempt (2) ran ALL 15,136 steps to schedule -- no early stop, no degrade-guard abort, last eval 1.46684 @15000. COMPLETED 2026-10-01 ~03:50 PDT. BEST val bpb 1.40325 @13400 = 1.76B tokens seen = 28.06 tok/param (train_tokens/params). On the matched-token harness it is 1.3947 vs pythia-70m@step1000 1.4715 = 5.2% AHEAD (commit a3a3b8b); that result supersedes this arm's earlier 'fail' framing. FIXTURE MOVED 2026-10-06 (the matched-token pair above is the OLD fixture): the 2.004B cache's val tail now lies inside the 160M run's training set, so the shared fixture became the tail of pile_train_full_bpe_pythia_hf.bin (32,366,957 ids, bpt 3.8743, resolved by scripts/val_fixture.py). Re-scored there on the same harness: ours 1.4735 vs pythia-70m@step1000 1.5680 = 6.0% AHEAD; at pythia's native ctx 2048 the gap is +0.0079 = a wash inside the regional sd. Verdict unchanged, numbers moved with the fixture. THE ARM'S OWN SUCCESS CRITERION IS MET, and it is the graded one, not the raw mark: the gap vs the Chinchilla fit SHRANK instead of growing, which was the stated failure mode that killed the eff-16k arm. Gap in nats (fit 1.36 bpb, 3.9104 bytes/token): +0.617 @2000 -> +0.161 @6400 (knee) -> +0.117 @13400 (best). Landed INSIDE the predicted +0.16..+0.22 population-regression band, then below it. THREE CAVEATS, because the headline number oversells: (1) THE 1.42 PASS MARK IS UNRESOLVABLE AT THIS EVAL CADENCE -- the eval at the anchor step 10800 reads 1.44055, a nominal MISS by 0.020, but median check-to-check |delta| is 0.03525 so the dashboard noise band is 0.141 wide; the mark sits deep inside noise. 9 of 75 evals did clear 1.42 (steps 6400/7400/8400/9400/10400/11400/12400/13400/14400). Call the mark neither passed nor failed; call the gap trend, which is resolvable, and it passed. (2) 'BEST 1.40325' IS A TROUGH, NOT A FLOOR -- val bpb oscillates periodically with amplitude ~0.037 (last 12 evals cycle 1.403<->1.477). The honest result is a BAND, roughly 1.403-1.477, not a point estimate. Do not quote the single best without the band. (3) THE EPOCH BOUGHT LESS THAN ITS LENGTH SUGGESTS -- the curve first beat 1.42 at step 6400 (42% of the schedule) and then spent 8,500 further steps oscillating flat inside that same band. Blocks of 10 evals show block-best 1.40652 @8200-10000, then 1.40352, 1.40325, 1.40374 for the last three blocks: no gain after step ~10k. The extra 60% of the epoch bought ~0.0003 bpb. Real finding for the next arm: the knee is data-limited, not step-limited, so a second epoch should be expected to buy very little; get the win from tokens or capacity instead. Served-vs-val stayed tight (served 1.4076 vs val 1.4032 at best), so the loader never recycled -- the plateau is the model, not the data feed.

ignore_dirs_note: 2026-09-29: unregistered dirs were classified, not blanket-ignored. Real evidence runs (m66m-4p5gb-40k, pythia-owt50kv2-lr-15e-4-long, pile-native-tok-200step) were registered as arms; the rest are calibration smokes (batch sweep for tok/s, 3-step ladder build checks, short 4k-vocab probes) plus one launch casualty. Calibration runs answer 'does it fit and how fast', not 'what did the model learn', so they carry no verdict and are ignored by name. 2026-09-30: three batch-ladder SMOKES (200 steps each, val_every 0) ignored by name - they measure throughput/VRAM, not val quality, so they carry no verdict. {"20260929_2249_pythia_tokenizer_pile_train_full": "ladder rung A smoke: eff 16k (micro16x2) lr 5e-4, 200 steps, 12,581MB peak, 71,527 tok/s - control", "20260929_2250_pythia_tokenizer_pile_train_full": "ladder rung B smoke: eff 131k (micro32x8) lr 1e-3, 200 steps, 16,001MB peak (98% of card), 18,556 tok/s - micro 32 thrashes the allocator", "20260930_0842_pythia_tokenizer_pile_train_full": "ladder rung C smoke: eff 131k (micro16x16) lr 5e-4, 200 steps, 12,017MB peak, 77,464 tok/s - the batch-alone arm, 8x batch at higher tps"}
